title: Measure a brake rotor's thickness with an outside micrometer
instruction: Measure the brake rotor's thickness with the outside micrometer, and leave the micrometer on the reading, back on its rest.
context: Automotive service technicians and mechanics (SOC 49-3023, about 0.7 million employed in the US, BLS OEWS approximate) measure brake rotor thickness at every brake job against the discard thickness stamped on the rotor. The standard tool is a 0-25 mm outside micrometer: one hand holds the frame square on the rotor's friction band and rocks it slightly across the face (the manufacturers' technique for finding the true, smallest reading), the other turns the ratchet knob until it clicks (it slips at the 5-10 N measuring force), then the micrometer is lifted off with the reading showing on the thimble.
setup: Left and right are the robot's. Positions in metres from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left, z up from the table. A 280 mm vented front brake rotor (fixed: 21.78 mm thick, worn from 22.0 mm, hat 40 mm deep, 36 vanes, 5 studs) stands on a bench hub stand, its axis along y at 0.152 m, centre x 0.508, y 0.120; its nearest rim is at x 0.368. A 0-25 mm outside micrometer of the Mitutoyo 103-137 class (free: 175 g, 18 mm thimble, 6.35 mm faces, 0.5 mm pitch, ratchet stop, lock lever, spindle fully open at 25.0 mm) lies across the two ribs of a bench rest at x 0.330, y 0.165, its axis along y, its throat opening toward +x.
scoring: Four steps, 0.2 each, judged as things stand at the end. (1) The micrometer was closed square on the rotor's friction band: its anvil face centre 100 to 136 mm from the hub axis, the anvil on the rotor's face (within 1 mm), its axis within 5 degrees of the hub axis, and the reading within +-0.02 mm of the rotor's 21.78 mm. (2) With step 1, the ratchet clicked (slipped a tooth) at least twice with the faces on the rotor. (3) With step 2, the micrometer is off the rotor and its reading is within +-0.02 mm of 21.78 mm. (4) With step 3, the micrometer lies on its rest (within 12 mm, 4 mm up, 6 degrees), no gripper holds it and no pad is within 3 cm. Full score 1.0 (ends the run) only once all four have held together for 1 s with the micrometer within 2 mm and 2 degrees of where it was when that second began; any lapse restarts the second, and the step points stop at 0.8. Scoring 0 for the whole run: the micrometer falling off the table, or dropped (falling faster than 0.6 m/s with nothing holding it).
reset_notes: Lay the micrometer across the rest's ribs with the spindle fully open (25.0 mm), the lock lever unlocked and the ratchet at rest. Nothing is held.
fidelity: Declared: the thread (the knob's turn moves the spindle 0.5 mm a turn), the ratchet (slips at 0.006 N m, a click per 18 degrees, estimates), the measuring force (6 N from a 0.03 mm lag; spindle drive capped at 10 N, the top of the real ratchet's 5-10 N spec). After the faces close the drive follows the spindle closing, never opening, so rocking settles the reading at its minimum. Band +-0.02 mm, never widened. Frame sizes, lever (unscored) are estimates.
scores: Dream-1 run: 0.0 (hit the step limit); demo: 1.0 at step 2815 (Isaac, scripted demo)
